name: RobStride 01
_comment_source: All figures from the RobStride RS01 User Manual (rev 260713), sections 1.2-1.4 and 2.1. Phase resistance, inductance, rotor inertia and the thermal network are NOT published and are estimated by the tool - see the ASSUMED PARAMETERS section of any report.

datasheet.title: RobStride RS01 User Manual
datasheet._note: revision is the vendor's filename stamp; version/date are from the manual's own section 7 Version History. The vendor's version field is inert: the 260713 revision STILL declares v1.0 dated 2025-11-25, seven months and several real spec changes after the 251210 revision did. The sha256 is the only reliable identity - verify with 'eval_actuator.py --check-datasheets'.

gear_eff.note: back-solving vendor Kt_out=1.22 against Ke=9.6 gives 0.99, which is not credible for a 7.75:1 planetary. Both Kt and Ke are quoted to 2 s.f., so the back-solve is degenerate here; class default retained instead. See notes.

Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM.note: manual 1.3.10 'motor back potential', line-to-line RMS per 1000 rotor rpm

kt_sat_derate.note: 17 N.m actual peak vs 19.8 N.m linear extrapolation of Kt at 23 Apk

V_bus_nom.note: RS01 is rated at 36 V, NOT 48 V like the rest of the family

tau_cont_out_spec.note: manual 1.2.3 'rated load (CW)'; ambient and mounting unspecified

T_winding_max.note: 260713 revision states 135 degC (actual insulation limit 180 degC). The 251210 revision had this and the RS02 the other way round; the newer revision is taken as the corrected one - a value that swaps between revisions is most likely an erratum that was caught and fixed.

notes: Vendor rated torque of 6 N.m is quoted with no stated ambient temperature or mounting condition, so it cannot be taken as a continuous rating in an enclosed robot arm. This tool computes the continuous limit from the thermal model instead.

The RS01 and RS02 are the same motor with different bus ratings: identical mass, dimensions, gear ratio, Ke, currents and torques. The RS02 is rated 48 V and reaches 410 rpm no-load; the RS01 is rated 36 V and reaches 315 rpm. Prefer the RS02 entry if your bus is 48 V.

gear_eff is a class default, not a back-solve. Kt_out (1.22) and Ke (9.6) are each given to 2 s.f., and back-solving one against the other implies 99% efficiency - inside the rounding band but not physically credible. Treat torque-per-amp predictions as +/-6%.
Datasheet no-load speed of 315 rpm at 36 V corresponds to 2441 rotor rpm, about 92% of the line-to-line RMS the bus can supply - consistent with the quoted Ke.
Dual 14-bit magnetic encoders, 1 Mbps CAN, FOC drive integrated. Class B insulation, -20 to 50 degC ambient, no-load current 0.5 Arms.
Housing is 63 mm dia x 28 mm per the 1.1 outline drawing. The 'Dimensions: 58mm' in the 2.1 driver table refers to the control board, not the actuator.

260713 revision adds the rated-load test setup: aluminium-alloy heat sink, 260 x 280 mm, rated load measured at 100 rpm output. The earlier 251210 revision left mounting entirely unqualified. A heat sink that size is a bench fixture, not a robot joint, so the vendor rated torque still should not be read as a continuous rating in an enclosed arm.

Vendor overload endurance (ROTATING and STALLED) is now carried as structured data in overload_curves below. NOTE the rotating table is byte-identical to the RS02's and is treated as a shared observation, not an independent one.

Stall is the case to watch for holding-torque duty: the manual states single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x that when rotating, because the three phases heat unevenly with the rotor stationary. The two-node thermal model assumes even heating and so reads optimistic against the stall table by construction - the report says so.
These endurance figures superseded the 251210 numbers, which differed materially (RS00 at 14 N.m: 5 s then, 3 s now). Any thermal-model fit should use the 260713 values.

tn_curve.note: No T-N curve is recorded for the RS01. Its manual prints one, but the plot spans 200-410 rpm and ends exactly at the RS02's 410 rpm no-load speed, 30% past the RS01's own 315 rpm at 36 V - so the curve was measured on the 48 V RS02 and pasted into both manuals. The RS01 appears to be the original part and the RS02 the later higher-voltage derivative, which is consistent with the newer measurement being reused backwards. The tool falls back to its computed envelope here.

overload_curves.note: 260713 manual overload endurance, rotating. CAUTION: this table is byte-identical to the RS02's, and the two manuals are known to share content (the RS01's printed T-N curve is the RS02's, and their winding limits were swapped between revisions). The RS01 is a 36 V part and the RS02 a 48 V part, so identical endurance at identical torques is plausible only if the table was measured once and reused. Treated as one observation shared with the RS02, not an independent one; tol widened to 0.20 accordingly. Their STALL tables do differ, which is itself evidence this rotating one was copied.

260713 manual overload endurance, stalled. Differs from the RS02's stall table, unlike the rotating one, so this appears to be genuinely the RS01's own measurement. Single-phase heating under stall is 1.414x rotating; the two-node model assumes even three-phase heating and will read optimistic here by construction.
